title: Your first home clean, without the extra homework
excerpt: A few small preparations help your cleaning team spend more time on the work you booked.

sections.heading: Start with your priorities
paragraphs: You do not need to clean your house before a cleaning visit. A more useful starting point is deciding which rooms or details matter most to you. Maybe it is the kitchen after a busy week, bathroom build-up, or the dust along the baseboards.

Share those priorities when requesting your quote. Mention any delicate finishes, items that should not be moved, or products you prefer. Clear instructions help the team understand your home before they arrive.

sections.heading: Make surfaces easy to reach
paragraphs: Put away loose clothing, toys and dishes where practical. This is about access, rather than making the house look perfect. A clear counter or floor lets the team reach the surface that needs cleaning.
Store important documents, valuables and personal items where you want them to stay. If a room should be left untouched, tell the team ahead of time.

sections.heading: Plan arrival and access
paragraphs: Confirm how the team will enter, whether you will be home, and how you want the property secured afterwards. Share door codes privately with the team rather than in a public message or review.
Let the team know about pets and arrange a comfortable place for them during the visit. If parking or building access needs special instructions, include those too.

sections.heading: Know what your first visit includes
paragraphs: New recurring Asepsis customers start with a Deep Clean before moving to regular Standard visits. This first visit gives the team time for the extra detail work that regular upkeep builds on.
Check the service description and any agreed add-ons before your appointment. At the end, use the walk-through to ask questions and point out anything you want the team to review.

title: Standard or Deep Clean: choosing the right starting point
excerpt: How everyday upkeep differs from a more detailed reset, and where move-out cleaning fits.
imageAlt: An uncluttered bathroom with a white bath

sections.heading: Standard is for regular upkeep
paragraphs: A Standard Clean focuses on the everyday work that helps a regularly cleaned home stay comfortable: kitchen and bathroom surfaces, reachable dusting, vacuuming, mopping, trash and beds in occupied homes.

It is a good starting point for understanding recurring service, but the condition of the home matters as much as the calendar. A home that has gone some time without a detailed clean may need a deeper first visit.

sections.heading: Deep adds attention to build-up
paragraphs: A Deep Clean includes Standard tasks and adds areas such as baseboards, doors, switches, fans, vents, blinds, sills and tracks. In kitchens and bathrooms, the extra detail includes the range hood, microwave interior, soap scum and grout.
For Asepsis recurring customers, that is the first visit. The regular Standard rate starts with the second visit. It is also an option for a one-time reset before guests or a change of season.

sections.heading: Move-out cleaning goes inside
paragraphs: Move-In / Move-Out cleaning is our most thorough residential option and is completed in an empty home. It adds appliance interiors, cabinets, drawers and closets to the Deep Clean scope.
Some tasks, such as interior window glass, are separate add-ons. Check the current service list and explain any unusual conditions so your quote reflects the work you actually need.

title: A weekly reset that fits real life
excerpt: A simple way to organise small household tasks between professional cleaning visits.
imageAlt: Neutral seating in a bright living room

sections.heading: Choose one repeatable moment
paragraphs: A home routine is easier to keep when it fits the week you already have. Choose a short, predictable moment to return loose items to their places, gather laundry and make a note of tasks that need more time.
Keep the list small enough to finish. The goal is a comfortable home, rather than a perfect room at the expense of your whole weekend.

sections.heading: Separate tidying from cleaning
paragraphs: Tidying puts belongings away. Cleaning works on surfaces. Treating them as separate tasks can help you decide what to do yourself and what to include in a professional visit.
Start with the places your household uses most. Clearing the dining table or returning shoes to one spot may make a bigger difference to your evening than reorganising an entire cupboard.

sections.heading: Keep a running list for your team
paragraphs: If you notice a detail that needs extra attention, add it to a short note for your next visit. Share the list in advance so the team can explain whether it is included or needs an add-on.
If your household routine changes, revisit your cleaning frequency. A useful schedule should support your life, including busy seasons, visitors and time away.

title: Moving out? Plan the clean around the move
excerpt: Work backwards from your handover date to make space for an empty-home clean.
imageAlt: Kitchen cabinets and a wooden island

sections.heading: Book around an empty home
paragraphs: Move-out cleaning works best after furniture, boxes and leftover belongings have been removed. Plan the visit after the moving crew has finished, with enough time before you return the keys to complete a walk-through.
Confirm that the team will have access to the property and the utilities needed for the agreed work. Tell them about any overlapping repairs or deliveries that could affect the visit.

sections.heading: Empty the interiors you want cleaned
paragraphs: Our Move-In / Move-Out service includes the interiors of appliances, cabinets, drawers and closets. Remove food, belongings and shelf contents beforehand so those spaces are ready.

Point out anything left behind intentionally. If you need a garage sweep-out or interior window glass cleaning, include that when requesting the quote rather than assuming it is part of the base service.

sections.heading: Leave room for a final check
paragraphs: Use the final walk-through to compare the work with your agreed scope. Keep your own move-out checklist separate from any building or landlord requirements, and share those requirements with the team early.
A professional clean is one part of a handover. It does not determine a landlord's inspection decision or deposit return, so make time for your other moving responsibilities too.

title: Make room for the week in your kitchen
excerpt: Three ways to make the busiest room easier to use and easier to clean.
imageAlt: Open kitchen counter space beside a stove

sections.heading: Give everyday items a home
paragraphs: A countertop often becomes a landing place for mail, bags and items that belong elsewhere. Choose a place for those items outside your main preparation area and return them there when you have a moment.
Leave the things you use most within reach. You do not need an empty kitchen to have a practical one; you need enough accessible space to do the things your household does every day.

sections.heading: Plan appliance interiors separately
paragraphs: Exterior appliance cleaning and interior cleaning are different tasks. Oven and refrigerator interiors are add-ons to our Standard and Deep services, while they are included in Move-In / Move-Out cleaning.
Ask about these tasks when booking. Agree in advance who will empty the appliance and how to prepare it, especially if you will not be home during the visit.

sections.heading: Tell us about your surfaces
paragraphs: Let your cleaning team know about delicate materials, recently installed finishes and any care instructions from the manufacturer. Keep those instructions handy instead of guessing which method will suit every surface.
The most helpful kitchen plan combines a manageable everyday routine with a clearly agreed professional cleaning scope.

title: A cleaning visit while you are out: what to arrange
excerpt: Access, pets and priorities: the details worth sharing before you head out.
imageAlt: A calm living area with plants and comfortable chairs

sections.heading: Agree on secure access
paragraphs: You do not have to stay home for every visit. Arrange entry directly with the team and confirm any instructions about doors, alarms or keys. Avoid placing sensitive access details in public reviews or social posts.
Make sure the team can contact you if something unexpected comes up, and agree on what to do if they cannot enter.

sections.heading: Make the boundaries clear
paragraphs: Tell the team which rooms to clean and which spaces or belongings should be left alone. Put away personal papers and valuables, and share any changes to the usual scope before arrival.
For pets, discuss a comfortable arrangement that keeps them away from the active work area. Tell the team about any doors or gates that must remain closed.

sections.heading: Confirm the finish
paragraphs: Agree on how the home should be secured after the visit. If you cannot join a walk-through, ask how to share any follow-up questions when you return.
Consistent instructions make future visits simpler. Update them whenever your household, access arrangements or cleaning priorities change.

title: Weekly, fortnightly or monthly: finding your rhythm
excerpt: Think about how your household uses its space before choosing a recurring schedule.
imageAlt: A bright bathroom with clear vanity surfaces

sections.heading: Start with your household
paragraphs: The right schedule depends on how you use your home. Think about which rooms are busy, how much upkeep you want to do yourself and the time you would like to free up.
A larger home does not automatically need a more frequent visit than a smaller one. Occupancy, pets, visitors and your own preferences all help shape a useful conversation with the cleaning team.

sections.heading: Compare the complete plan
paragraphs: Look at the service scope alongside the per-visit price. A recurring Standard Clean is designed for regular upkeep, with a Deep Clean at the beginning to establish the starting point.
Use the residential pricing page to compare the published rates for your home size, and include any extra bathrooms, additional floor area or optional tasks in your estimate.

sections.heading: Adjust when life changes
paragraphs: A cleaning schedule should be useful, not another chore to manage. If a new routine, guests or travel changes your needs, speak with the team about the next available options.
Ask directly about rescheduling arrangements before making a commitment. Clear expectations make it easier to choose a rhythm that works for everyone.

title: What to include in a commercial cleaning enquiry
excerpt: A clear project brief helps your contractor understand the space, schedule and handover.
imageAlt: Illustrative interior with cabinets and clean work surfaces

sections.heading: Describe the space and the work
paragraphs: Start with the property type, city, approximate square footage and the service you need. Office janitorial work, a tenant turnover and a construction final clean each involve a different scope.
Mention any special access requirements, surface materials or areas that should be excluded. Plans and photos can help the team understand the site before arranging a walk-through.

sections.heading: Share the schedule
paragraphs: For recurring work, describe your preferred frequency and the hours when the space is available. For construction, share the expected completion and handover dates, plus any phases you want priced separately.
If other trades will still be working, explain how their schedule may overlap with cleaning. A clear sequence helps define what counts as the final handover condition.

sections.heading: Name the contact and the decision point
paragraphs: Include the person coordinating access and the person reviewing the quote. Let the team know if your vendor process requires a certificate of insurance, W-9 or a particular scope format.
Commercial and project enquiries go to Asepsis Edmond at asepsisedmond@gmail.com. Residential customers should use the home-cleaning contact option on the website.
